title: Input and output models, validation and response_model
summary: Separate the schemas: what comes in, what goes out and what gets stored.

sections.definition: Separate the schemas: what comes in (ClienteCrear), what goes out (ClientePublico) and what gets stored. The endpoint's return type, or response_model, validates and filters the response: only the fields of the output model go out.
sections.analogy: The menu the customer sees doesn't show the cost of the ingredients or the supplier, even though the kitchen knows them.
sections.problem: With a single model for everything you end up returning the password hash or letting the client send fields it shouldn't, like es_admin.
sections.code:example:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, EmailStr, Field

class ClienteBase(BaseModel):
    nombre: str = Field(min_length=2)
    email: EmailStr

class ClienteCrear(ClienteBase):
    password: str = Field(min_length=8)

class ClientePublico(ClienteBase):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)   # para leer objetos ORM
    id: int

@app.post("/clientes", status_code=201)
def crear_cliente(datos: ClienteCrear, session: SessionDep) -> ClientePublico:
    cliente = guardar_cliente(session, datos)   # tiene hashed_password
    return cliente                              # sale solo id, nombre, email

# Si devuelves un tipo distinto al anotado, usa response_model
@app.get("/clientes/{cliente_id}", response_model=ClientePublico)
def obtener_cliente(cliente_id: int, session: SessionDep):
    return session.get(Cliente, cliente_id)
sections.bad:
@app.post("/clientes")
def crear(datos: ClienteCrear) -> ClienteCrear:
    guardar(datos)
    return datos            # devuelve el password

The input model is used as the output.
sections.good:
@app.post("/clientes", status_code=201)
def crear(datos: ClienteCrear) -> ClientePublico:
    return guardar(datos)   # FastAPI filtra

Separate input and output; inheritance avoids repeating fields.
sections.bridge:typescript: It's the idea of DTOs: having a CreateClienteDto type for what comes in and a ClienteResponse for what goes out. The difference is that here the output model isn't just a type: it's validated and filtered at runtime. Pydantic versus a TS interface: the interface disappears at compile time; the model acts.
sections.interview: I define different models for input and output, usually with a shared base class. The input validates what the client can send and the output controls what I expose: if I annotate the return type or use response_model, FastAPI filters the fields, so a password hash never leaks. If the body doesn't comply, the client gets a 422 with the details; if my response doesn't comply, it's a 500 because it's a server error.
sections.myths:
• Using the same model for input, output and the table.
  • Returning an ORM object without from_attributes=True.
  • If your response doesn't match the output model, the error is a 500 (your bug), not a 422.
  • By default extra fields are ignored; with model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid") you reject them.

exercises.prompt: Which status code does it return?

items.q: The handler returns a dict without the id field, which is required in ClientePublico.
items.why: Response validation fails (ResponseValidationError). It's a server error: 500.

items.q: What does FastAPI do with fields that aren't in the output model?
items.why: The response model works as a filter: only what's declared goes out.
